title: Christ, for Thee a Wreath Adorning
description: Christ, for Thee a Wreath Adorning in Tonic Solfa to OMNI DIE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), and this page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Christ, for Thee a wreath a-dorn-ing Weaves my rap-tured soul with glee, For from death this glo-rious morn-ing Thou hast ri-sen tri-umphant-ly.

lines: Christ, for Thee a wreath adorning
Weaves my raptured soul with glee,
For from death this glorious morning
Thou hast risen triumphantly.
From the tomb behold Him rising,
Christ our Lord whose praise is sung.
Death is slain; O power surprising!
Hades' gates are open flung.
Thou for man to earth in meekness
Cam'st that he new born might be;
Thou upon the cross in weakness
Diedst that he might die with Thee.
Thou didst rise — we hail Thee, Jesus!
And we leave the tomb with Thee.
Victor, by the power that frees us,
Where Thou art, there we would be.
Hark! the highest heavens are ringing,
Choirs angelic lead the strain,
And my opened lips in singing
Tell the praises forth again.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to OMNI DIE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
